result.text: A university enrollment system involves the following steps: Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes: Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes: Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use bpmn:subProcess for a nested workflow belonging to its parent process; keep all internal nodes and flows inside it.

result.rule: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.

When the description states a sequence of activities or a conditional step followed by a later activity: Connect the activities and any modeled gateways in the stated order with sequence flows, including every described transition.

When the description makes completion contingent on both a time-based condition and a separate required activity, without stating that one must precede the other.: Model the time-based wait with an intermediate catch event and the activity as a parallel branch; synchronize the branches with a parallel gateway before completion.

When the description states that a condition or decision leads to a distinct action before subsequent work: Model the action as a separate task on the corresponding branch, and connect it to the preceding and subsequent work as described, including any return flow.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.

When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.

When the description gives an activity together with contextual or explanatory details that are not needed to distinguish the activity in its process context: Label the BPMN task with its core action and necessary object, omitting redundant contextual modifiers while preserving details essential to the activity’s meaning.
When the description specifies multiple distinct actions within one activity: label the BPMN activity so that it communicates each stated action, rather than omitting one
